About Equip 

Equip is the leading virtual, evidence-based eating disorder treatment program on a mission to ensure that everyone with an eating disorder can access treatment that works. Created by clinical experts in the field and people with lived experience, Equip builds upon evidence-based treatments to empower individuals to reach lasting recovery. All Equip patients receive a dedicated care team, including a therapist, dietitian, physician, and peer and family mentor. The company operates in all 50 states and is partnered with most major health insurance plans. Learn more about our strong outcomes and treatment approach at www.equip.health.

Founded in 2019, Equip has been a fully virtual company since its inception and is proud of the highly-engaged, passionate, and diverse Equipsters that have created Equip’s culture.  Recognized by Time as one of the most influential companies of 2023, along with awards from Linkedin and Lattice, we are grateful to Equipsters for building a sustainable treatment program that has served thousands of patients and families.

About the role

Equip is seeking a strategic, human-centered Director, Patient Engagement & Behavioral Insights to lead how we understand, design and improve the end-to-end experience of patients and families in treatment. Reporting to the VP of Patient Journey, this leader will oversee insights, service design and content. They will work closely with our clinical and operational partners to find and deliver the improvements that matter most for engagement, retention and outcomes.

In this role, timely high impact content is the core product. It reaches patients and families in our app, through lifecycle channels like messaging, email and push, and inside care sessions as talking points, guidance and follow-up actions taken by care teams. This role sees all of those as one system. You’ll run end-to-end service design work and real-world experiments across digital and human touchpoints to learn where to invest, then turn those insights into scaled changes.

You love working where art meets science. You think critically about evidence: how strong it is, the context it came from, and whether it applies to our patients. Then you think broadly about what it means for the experience you own. You favor fast, iterative learning in the real world over perfect plans, and you build trust with clinical and operational teams by making their work easier and better. You measure the success of timely content not by clicks or views but rather by how effectively it drives engagement, treatment, and experience outcomes.

Responsibilities

  • Build, mentor and unite a team that spans user research, behavioral insights, and CRM/lifecycle, with clear roles and ways of working.

  • Own and oversee the insights function, including our Patient & Family Advisory Council and lived-experience research panels. Support your insights team in setting an effective research agenda and roadmap, keep quality high, and make sure what patients and families tell us shapes roadmaps, content and operating decisions.

  • Map the patient and family journey across the app, lifecycle channels, conversational AI interactions, care sessions and care team workflows. Find the moments that drive engagement and drop-off, and set priorities for improvement based on impact and evidence.

  • Plan campaigns ahead of time around the moments that matter most in treatment, such as milestones, transitions, high-risk periods and family touchpoints. Make sure each campaign is coordinated across the app, lifecycle channels and care sessions.

  • Set up an agile workflow that uses AI tools, including Claude Design, to draft, design, test and refine campaign content quickly. Partner with the Creative team on brand standards and high-visibility work, and keep clinical review built into the process.

  • Set strategy and standards for patient and family content wherever it’s delivered: in the app, through lifecycle messaging, and in sessions through talking points, guidance and care team follow-up.

  • Define and own the in-treatment voice, creating evaluation standards, content guidelines and overseeing conversational design for agentic experiences. Develop the infrastructure and processes to develop and deploy high impact in treatment content

  • Set up a learning plan that combines A/B tests, pilots, service blueprints and operational trials. Choose methods that fit the question, de-risk the highest risk areas and turn results into decisions quickly.

  • Own our lifecycle and orchestration strategy (currently operated by Braze platform), including journey orchestration, segmentation, triggering and measurement. Partner with Engineering and Data on capabilities and integrations.

  • Work with Product, Clinical and Engineering to decide which content experiences should stay deterministic (rule-based and clinically reviewed) and which should become adaptive or AI-driven. Set the evidence, safety and quality bar for those transitions. Partner with Product and Engineering to move outreach to a next best action framework.

  • Partner closely with Clinical and Care Operations to design changes that work in practice for care teams. Co-own rollout, adoption and measurement of new session workflows and follow-up actions.

  • Bring frameworks like habit formation, motivation, choice architecture and family systems into design. Test them in context, and stay honest when the evidence doesn’t hold up for our population.

  • Define and track success metrics for engagement, retention and content effectiveness, connected to clinical and business outcomes, alongside our Data team.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in applied behavioral science (in a real world setting, ideally a business setting), research and insights, service design, or patient/consumer engagement, including 4+ years leading teams that span more than one of these disciplines.

  • Demonstrated leadership experience translating insights into actionable content strategy

  • A background in behavioral science, applied research or insights, with a track record of turning evidence into content, design and business decisions.

  • Hands-on experience leading end-to-end service design across digital and human-delivered touchpoints. Healthcare, behavioral health or other high-touch services strongly preferred.

  • A strong experimentation mindset: you’ve designed and run real-world tests and pilots, including in operational settings where clean A/B tests aren’t possible.

  • Skill at judging evidence critically: you understand research design, generalizability and context, and you can explain uncertainty clearly to clinical and executive audiences.

  • Experience owning lifecycle programs and knowledge of content management systems.

  • Experience running advisory councils, research panels or community-based research, ideally with patients, families or people with lived experience.

  • Familiarity with AI-enabled or adaptive content experiences, and good judgment about where personalization helps and where consistency and clinical safety come first.

  • Strong partnership skills with clinical and operational leaders, and comfort working in a fast-paced, matrixed, clinical-first startup.

  • Demonstrated interest in eating disorders, mental health or family-based care.

Benefits:

Time Off:

  • Flex PTO policy (3-5 wks/year recommended) + 11 paid company holidays.

  • Generous parental leave.

Core Benefits:

  • Competitive Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, and AD&D insurance.

    • Equip pays for a significant percentage of benefits premiums for individuals and families.

  • Spring Health, a 100% employer-paid mental health benefit through Guardian.

    • You can receive 5 free therapy sessions and 5 free coaching sessions per year for you and each of your dependents.

  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP), a company paid resource for mental health, legal services, financial support, and more!

  • HealthJoy, a 100% employer-paid platform connecting you to a healthcare concierge who can help you navigate your benefits.

  • 401K Option!

Other Benefits

Work From Home Additional Perks:

  • $50/month stipend added directly to an employee’s paycheck to cover home internet expenses.

  • $250/month stipend to use a co-working space.

  • Initial work-from-home stipend of up to $500.

    • Reload of $200 on the home office stipend at the 3-year mark and then every other year after that (year 5, year 7, etc.).

  • Company Laptop.

Physical Demands

Work is performed 100% from home with limited travel for team meetings. Must be able to remain in a stationary period for prolonged periods at a desk or workstation, with the option to alternate between sitting and standing as needed. Must be able to operate standard office equipment such as a computer screen and keyboards as well as to exchange accurate information, actively listen, and communicate clearly with colleagues, clients or stakeholders over the phone, via video conferencing, and/or in person.

At Equip, Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) are woven into everything we do. At the heart of Equip’s mission is a relentless dedication to making sure that everyone with an eating disorder has access to care that works regardless of race, gender, sexuality, ability, weight, socio-economic status, and any marginalized identity. We also strive toward our providers and corporate team reflecting that same dedication both in bringing in and retaining talented employees from all backgrounds and identities. We have an Equip DEIB council, Equip For All; also referred to as EFA. EFA at Equip aims to be a space driven by mutual respect, and thoughtful, effective communication strategy - enabling full participation of  members who identify as marginalized or under-represented and allies, amplifying diverse voices, creating opportunities for advocacy and contributing to the advancement of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging at Equip.

As an equal opportunity employer, we provide equal opportunity in all aspects of employment, including recruiting, hiring, compensation, training and promotion, termination, and any other terms and conditions of employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, familial status, age, disability, weight, and/or any other legally protected classification protected by federal, state, or local law. 

Our dedication to equitable access, which is core to our mission, extends to how we build our "village." In line with our commitment to Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB), we are dedicated to an accessible hiring process where all candidates feel a true sense of belonging. If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete your application, interview, or perform the essential functions of a role, we invite you to reach out to our People team at accommodations@equip.health.
